Area.evidence_source: [/page/9/Text/7] This qualitative study, by exploring the experiences of older people who had recently acted on their suicidal feelings, represents a move away from more traditional approaches focused on retrospective measurement of risk factors and epidemiological trends. This study has shown three broad themes to be pertinent to the experience of participants around the time of their suicide attempt—Struggle, Control and Visibility. However, the diversity of experience at this time indicates the need to consider the perspective of the individual and the surrounding social context rather than searching for a clinical profile or 'stereotype' of an older person who is most at risk of attempted suicide. Overall, the present findings provide an insight into how older people may feel around the time of a suicide attempt and highlight what they see as being important.
